nodes.title: Edit instruction
Velocity Rig
widgets_values:
# Velocity Rig: fast-paced camera-rig car race
Pick a **hero car**, a **rival car**, a **world** and a **camera rig**, press **Run**: one 2-4 s shot with LTX-2.5's own engine sound.

**Rigs**: wheel cam (front / rear), door mount, bumper cam, rear bumper (reverse), roof cam, exhaust close-up,
arm car chase, arm car orbit, FPV drone dive / chase, top-down drone, helicopter wide, roadside whip pan,
low pass-by, crash zoom. **Worlds**: mountain pass, coastal cliffs, city night / day / tunnel, desert canyon,
forest gravel, snow mountain, rain docklands, race circuit, or type your own.

**Full race sequence**: leave rig on *auto (race sequence)*, set **shot_index** to *increment*, then queue 6-8 runs.
Every run advances the race arc (launch -> bumper draft -> hard brake -> wheel-cam hairpin -> FPV drift -> door-mount overtake -> reverse bumper defense -> whip-pan finish) and switches camera rigs.

nodes.title: Your car
widgets_values: **Qwen Image Edit 2511** (Lightning, 4 steps) re-shoots your car photo from the rig's position: same body, paint and wheels, new camera, new world. Use one clean photo of the car for every shot so it stays the same car.

nodes.title: Motion
widgets_values: **LTX-2.5 22B distilled**, image to video in two stages (half-res pass, x2 latent upscale, refine), with **synchronized audio**: the engine, tires and wind come from the same model. Size, length and fps all come from the rig node.

nodes.title: Speed FX
widgets_values: **Velocity FX** adds what a real rig adds: vibration, radial speed blur that keeps the car sharp, crash zoom, lens fringing and speed ramps, using each rig's own defaults. Sliders at -1 follow the rig; strength 0 bypasses it. Frame count never changes, so the LTX audio stays in sync. Both the raw and the FX clip are saved.
